Let $y$ be the number of 9-digit numbers formed using the digits of the set $S$ such that only two digits are repeated and each of these is repeated exactly twice. Then :
Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\frac{dy}{dx} - \sin 2y = x^{3}\left(2 - x^{3}\right)\cos^{2}y$, $x \ne 0$. If $y(2) = 0$, then $\tan(y(1))$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x\frac{dy}{dx} - \sin 2y = x^{3}\left(2 - x^{3}\right)\cos^{2}y$
$\frac{1}{\cos^{2}y}\frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{1}{x}\frac{2\sin y\cos y}{\cos^{2}y} = x^{2}\left(2 - x^{3}\right)$
$\sec^{2}y\frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{1}{x}(2\tan y) = x^{2}\left(2 - x^{3}\right)$
Let $\tan y = z$
$\sec^{2}y\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dz}{dx}$
$\frac{dz}{dx} - \frac{2}{x}z = x^{2}\left(2 - x^{3}\right)$
$\text{I.F.} = e^{-\int\frac{2}{x}dx} \Rightarrow e^{-2\ln|x|} = \frac{1}{x^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow z\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right) = \int x^{2}\left(2 - x^{3}\right) \times \frac{1}{x^{2}}dx$
$\frac{z}{x^{2}} = 2x - \frac{x^{4}}{4} + C$
$\frac{\tan y}{x^{2}} = 2x - \frac{x^{4}}{4} + C$
$y(2) = 0$
$0 = 4 - \frac{16}{4} + C \Rightarrow C = 0$
$\frac{\tan y}{x^{2}} = 2x - \frac{x^{4}}{4}$
$\tan y = 2x^{3} - \frac{x^{6}}{4}$
$y(1) = ?,\ x = 1$
$\tan(y(1)) = 2 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{7}{4}$

questions.stem: Let A, B and C be three $2 \times 2$ matrices with real entries such that $B = (I + A)^{-1}$ and $A + C = I$. If $BC = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $CB\begin{bmatrix} x_{1} \\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 12 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix}$, then $x_{1} + x_{2}$ is :
questions.solution:
$B = (I + A)^{-1}$
pre multiply by $(I + A)$
$(I + A)B = (I + A)(I + A)^{-1}$
$B + AB = I$ ..........(1)
post multiply by $(I + A)$
$B(I + A) = (I + A)^{-1}(I + A)$
$B + BA = I$ ..........(2)
from (1) and (2)
$AB = BA$
Now $A + C = I$
pre multiply by $B$: $BA + BC = B$ ..........(3)
post multiply by $B$: $AB + CB = B$ ..........(4)
from (3) and (4): $BC = CB$
Now $BC = CB = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_{1} \\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 12 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix}$
$x_{1} - 5x_{2} = 12,\quad -x_{1} + 2x_{2} = -6$
$x_{1} = -2,\ x_{2} = 2$

For three unit vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ satisfying $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^{2} + |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^{2} + |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^{2} = 9$ and $|2\vec{a} + k\vec{b} + k\vec{c}| = 3$, the positive value of $k$ is :
questions.solution:
$\left|\vec{a} + \vec{b}\right|^{2} + \left|\vec{b} - \vec{c}\right|^{2} + \left|\vec{c} - \vec{a}\right|^{2} = 9$
$2\left(a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}\right) - 2\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\right) = 9$
$2 \times 3 - 2\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\right) = 9$
$3 + 2\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\right) = 0$
$\left(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}\right)^{2} = 0$
So $\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = 0$
$\vec{b} + \vec{c} = -\vec{a}$
Now $|2\vec{a} + k(\vec{b} + \vec{c})| = 3$
$|(2 - k)\vec{a}| = 3$
$|2 - k| = 3$
$2 - k = \pm 3$
$k = -1,\ k = 5$

questions.stem: If $\frac{\tan(A - B)}{\tan A} + \frac{\sin^{2}C}{\sin^{2}A} = 1$, $A, B, C \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then :
questions.solution:
$\frac{\tan(A - B)}{\tan A} + \frac{\sin^{2}C}{\sin^{2}A} = 1$
$\frac{\tan A - \tan B}{(1 + \tan A\tan B)\tan A} + \frac{\mathrm{cosec}^{2}A}{\mathrm{cosec}^{2}C} = 1$
$\frac{\tan A - \tan B}{(1 + \tan A\tan B)\tan A} + \frac{1 + \cot^{2}A}{1 + \cot^{2}C} = 1$
Let $\tan A = x,\ \tan B = y,\ \tan C = z$
$\frac{x - y}{(1 + xy)x} + \frac{1 + \frac{1}{x^{2}}}{1 + \frac{1}{z^{2}}} = 1$
$\frac{x - y}{x(1 + xy)} + \frac{z^{2}\left(x^{2} + 1\right)}{x^{2}\left(z^{2} + 1\right)} = 1$
after solving we will get
$z^{2} = xy$
So $\tan^{2}C = \tan A \cdot \tan B$
$\tan A, \tan C, \tan B$ are in G.P.

options.text: $\tan A, \tan C, \tan B$, are in A.P.
$\tan A, \tan C, \tan B$, are in G.P.
$\tan A, \tan B, \tan C$, are in G.P.
$\tan A, \tan B, \tan C$, are in A.P.

Let ABC be an equilateral triangle with orthocenter at the origin and the side BC on the line $x + 2\sqrt{2}y = 4$. If the co-ordinates of the vertex A are $(\alpha, \beta)$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $\left|\alpha + \sqrt{2}\beta\right|$ is :
questions.solution:
$G(0, 0)$ is centroid/orthocenter; $BC : x + 2\sqrt{2}y + 4 = 0$
$= \frac{x - 0}{1} = \frac{y - 0}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{-1(0 + 0 + 4)}{9}$
$\frac{x}{1} = \frac{y}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{-4}{9}$
$x = \frac{-4}{9},\ y = \frac{-8\sqrt{2}}{9}$
$D\left(-\frac{4}{9}, \frac{-8\sqrt{2}}{9}\right)$; $A(\alpha, \beta)$, $G(0,0)$ divide $AD$ in $2 : 1$
$\frac{\alpha - \frac{8}{9}}{3} = 0,\ \frac{\beta - \frac{16\sqrt{2}}{9}}{3} = 0$
$\alpha = \frac{8}{9},\quad \beta = \frac{16\sqrt{2}}{9}$
Now $\left|\alpha + \sqrt{2}\beta\right| = \left|\frac{8}{9} + \frac{32}{9}\right| = \left|\frac{40}{9}\right| = 4.4$
$[4.4] = 4$

questions.stem: If $\int\left(\frac{1 - 5\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{5}x\cos^{2}x}\right)dx = f(x) + C$, where C is the constant of integration, then $f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) - f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\int\frac{1 - 5\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{5}x\cos^{2}x}dx = f(x) + c$
$\int\frac{\sec^{2}x}{\sin^{5}x}dx - \int\frac{5}{\sin^{5}x}dx$
Integration by parts
$\int\underset{\mathrm{II}}{\sec^{2}x}\;\underset{\mathrm{I}}{\frac{1}{\sin^{5}x}}dx - \int\frac{5}{\sin^{5}x}dx$
$\frac{1}{\sin^{5}x}\tan x - \int\frac{-1}{\left(\sin^{5}x\right)^{2}} \times 5\sin^{4}x\cos x\tan x\,dx - \int\frac{5}{\sin^{5}x}dx + C$
$\frac{\tan x}{\sin^{5}x} + \int\frac{5}{\sin^{5}x}dx - \int\frac{5}{\sin^{5}x}dx + C$
So $f(x) = \frac{\tan x}{\sin^{5}x}$
Now $f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) - f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\tan\pi/6}{(\sin\pi/6)^{5}} - \frac{\tan\pi/4}{(\sin\pi/4)^{5}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3} \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{5}} - \frac{1}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{5}}$
$\frac{32}{\sqrt{3}} - 4\sqrt{2}$
$\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\left(8 - \sqrt{6}\right)$

questions.stem: If the distances of the point $(1, 2, a)$ from the line $\frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{1}$ along the lines $L_{1} : \frac{x - 1}{3} = \frac{y - 2}{4} = \frac{z - a}{b}$ and $L_{2} : \frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{4} = \frac{z - a}{c}$ are equal, then $a + b + c$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let equation of line AB $\vec{r} = (1, 2, a) + \lambda(3, 4, b)$
So $B(1 + 3\lambda, 2 + 4\lambda, a + \lambda b)$ lies on line BC So
$\frac{1 + 3\lambda - 1}{1} = \frac{2 + 4\lambda}{2} = \frac{a + \lambda b - 1}{a}$
So $\lambda = 1$ and $a + b - 1 = 3$
equation line AC $\vec{r} = (1, 2, a) + \mu(1, 4, c)$
So $C(1 + \mu, 2 + 4\mu, a + \mu c)$ lies on line BC so
$\frac{1 + \mu - 1}{1} = \frac{2 + 4\mu}{2} = \frac{a + \mu c - 1}{a}$
$\mu = -1$, $a - c - 1 = -1 \Rightarrow a = c$
$B(4, 6, 4)$, $C(0, -2, 0)$
$AB^{2} = AC^{2}$
$9 + 16 + (a - 4)^{2} = 1 + 16 + a^{2}$
$a = 3,\ c = 3,\ b = 1$
$a + b + c = 7$

questions.stem: The value of $\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{\log_{e}\left(\sec(ex) \cdot \sec\left(e^{2}x\right) \cdot \ldots \cdot \sec\left(e^{10}x\right)\right)}{e^{2} - e^{2\cos x}}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{\log_{e}\left(\sec(ex)\sec\left(e^{2}x\right)\ldots\sec e^{10}x\right)}{e^{2} - e^{2\cos x}}$
$\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{\ln(\sec ex) + \ln\left(\sec\left(e^{2}x\right)\right) + \cdots \ln\left(\sec\left(e^{10}x\right)\right)}{e^{2\cos x}\left(e^{2 - 2\cos x} - 1\right)}$
$\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{\ln(\sec x) + \ln\left(\sec e^{2}x\right) + \cdots \ln\left(\sec e^{10}x\right)}{e^{2} \times (2 - 2\cos x)}$
$\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{-\ln(\cos x)}{e^{2}(2 - 2\cos x)} - \frac{\ln\left(\cos e^{2}x\right)}{e^{2}(2 - 2\cos x)}\cdots\frac{-\ln\left(\cos e^{10}x\right)}{e^{2}(2 - 2\cos x)}$
$\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{-(\cos x - 1)}{e^{2}(2(1 - \cos x))} \cdot \frac{\left(\cos^{2}x - 1\right)}{e^{2}(2(1 - \cos x))}\cdots\frac{-\left(\cos e^{10}x - 1\right)}{e^{2}(2(1 - \cos x))}$
$\left(\lim_{x \to 0}+\frac{(ex)^{2}}{2 \times 2\left(\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right)} + \frac{\left(e^{2}x\right)^{2}}{2 \times 2\left(\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right)} + \cdots\frac{\left(e^{10}x\right)^{2}}{2 \times 2\left(\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right)}\right)$
$\frac{1}{e^{2}}\left(\frac{e^{2}}{2} + \frac{e^{4}}{2} + \cdots\frac{e^{20}}{2}\right)$
$\frac{1}{2}\frac{1}{e^{2}}\frac{e^{2}\left(e^{20} - 1\right)}{e^{2} - 1} = \frac{e^{20} - 1}{2\left(e^{2} - 1\right)}$

questions.stem: The mean and variance of 10 observations are 9 and 34.2, respectively. If 8 of these observations are 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 13, 15, 21, then the mean deviation about the median of all the 10 observations is :

If $\alpha, \beta$, where $\alpha < \beta$, are the roots of the equation $\lambda x^{2} - (\lambda + 3)x + 3 = 0$ such that $\frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{\beta} = \frac{1}{3}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is :
questions.solution:
$\lambda x^{2} - (\lambda + 3)x + 3 = 0$
$\alpha + \beta = \frac{\lambda + 3}{\lambda},\quad \alpha\beta = \frac{3}{\lambda}$
$\frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{\beta} = \frac{1}{3}$
$\frac{\beta - \alpha}{\alpha\beta} = \frac{1}{3}$
$\frac{\sqrt{(\lambda + 3)^{2} - 12\lambda}}{|\lambda| \times \frac{3}{\lambda}} = \frac{1}{3}$
Sq. $(\lambda + 3)^{2} - 12\lambda = 1$
$\lambda^{2} + 9 + 6\lambda - 12\lambda = 1$
$\lambda^{2} - 6\lambda + 8 = 0$
sum $= 6$

questions.stem: Let $y = x$ be the equation of a chord of the circle $C_{1}$ (in the closed half-plane $x \ge 0$) of diameter 10 passing through the origin. Let $C_{2}$ be another circle described on the given chord as its diameter. If the equation of the chord of the circle $C_{2}$, which passes through the point $(2, 3)$ and is farthest from the center of $C_{2}$, is $x + ay + b = 0$, then $a - b$ is equal to :

Let $S = \left\{x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c : a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}\ \text{and}\ a, b, c \le 20\right\}$ be a set of polynomials. Then the number of polynomials in S, which are divisible by $x^{2} + 2$, is :
questions.solution:
$x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c$ is divisible by $x^{2} + 2$
So $x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + 2 = x\left(x^{2} + 2\right) + a\left(x^{2} + 2\right) + (b - 2)x + (c - 2a)$ is divisible by $x^{2} + 2$
So $b - 2 = 0$ and $c - 2a = 0$
$b = 2$ and $c = 2a$
$a = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 10$ with $b = 2$ and $c = 2, 4, 6, \ldots, 20$
So total polynomials $= 10$

questions.stem: In a G.P., if the product of the first three terms is 27 and the set of all possible values for the sum of its first three terms is $\mathbb{R} - (a, b)$, then $a^{2} + b^{2}$ is equal to __________.
questions.solution:
Let 3 terms be $\frac{a}{r}, a, ar$
$\frac{a}{r} \times a \times ar = 27$
$a^{3} = 27$
$a = 3$
Sum $= \frac{3}{r} + 3 + 3r$
$\Rightarrow 3\left(r + \frac{1}{r} + 1\right)$
Range of $r + \frac{1}{r} \in (-\infty, -2] \cup [2, \infty)$
$r + \frac{1}{r} + 1 \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [3, \infty)$
$3\left(r + \frac{1}{r} + 1\right) \in (-\infty, -3] \cup [9, \infty)$
so $3\left(r + \frac{1}{r} + 1\right) \in \mathbb{R} - (-3, 9)$
$a = -3,\ b = 9$
$a^{2} + b^{2} = 9 + 81 = 90$

questions.stem: For some $\theta \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2}\sec^{2}\theta = 8$ be $e_{1}$ and $l_{1}$, respectively, and let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $x^{2}\sec^{2}\theta + y^{2} = 6$ be $e_{2}$ and $l_{2}$, respectively. If $e_{1}^{2} = e_{2}^{2}\left(\sec^{2}\theta + 1\right)$, then $\left(\frac{l_{1}l_{2}}{e_{1}e_{2}}\right)\tan^{2}\theta$ is equal to __________.
questions.solution:
$x^{2} - y^{2}\sec^{2}\theta = 8$
$\frac{x^{2}}{8} - \frac{y^{2}}{8\cos^{2}\theta} = 1$
$e_{1} = \sqrt{1 + \frac{8\cos^{2}\theta}{8}} = \sqrt{1 + \cos^{2}\theta}$
$l_{1} = \frac{2b^{2}}{a} = \frac{2 \times 8\cos^{2}\theta}{2\sqrt{2}} = 4\sqrt{2}\cos^{2}\theta$
$\frac{x^{2}}{6\cos^{2}\theta} + \frac{y^{2}}{6} = 1$
$e_{2} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{6\cos^{2}\theta}{6}} = \sqrt{1 - \cos^{2}\theta}$
$l_{2} = \frac{2 \times 6\cos^{2}\theta}{\sqrt{6}} = 2\sqrt{6}\cos^{2}\theta$
Now $e_{1}^{2} = e_{2}^{2}\left(\sec^{2}\theta + 1\right)$
$1 + \cos^{2}\theta = \left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right)\left(\frac{1 + \cos^{2}\theta}{\cos^{2}\theta}\right)$
$\cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \cos^{2}\theta$
$\cos^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{2}$
So, $e_{1} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},\ l_{1} = 2\sqrt{2},\ e_{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}},\ l_{2} = \sqrt{6}$
$\Rightarrow \left(\frac{l_{1}l_{2}}{e_{1}e_{2}}\right)\tan^{2}\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \times \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}} \times 1$
$\Rightarrow 4 \times 2 = 8$

questions.stem: The value of $\sum_{r=1}^{20}\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{\pi\left(\int_{0}^{r} x\,|\sin\pi x|\,dx\right)}\right\rfloor\right)$ is __________.

If $k = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\right) + \tan\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\right)$, then the number of solutions of the equation $\sin^{-1}(kx - 1) = \sin^{-1}x - \cos^{-1}x$ is __________.
questions.solution:
$k = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\right) + \tan\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\right)$
$= \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\right) + \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\right)$
Let $\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{2}{3} = \theta \Rightarrow \cos 2\theta = \frac{2}{3}$
$\Rightarrow \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) + \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)$
$\frac{1 + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} + \frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}$
$k = 2\left(\frac{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}{1 - \tan^{2}\theta}\right) = \frac{2}{\cos 2\theta} = \frac{2}{2/3} = 3$
$\sin^{-1}(3x - 1) = \sin^{-1}x - \cos^{-1}x$
$\sin^{-1}(3x - 1) = 2\sin^{-1}x - \frac{\pi}{2}$
taking sin both side
$\sin\left(\sin^{-1}(3x - 1)\right) = \sin\left(2\sin^{-1}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$
$3x - 1 = -\cos\left(2\sin^{-1}x\right)$
Let $\sin^{-1}x = \theta$, $x = \sin\theta$
$3x - 1 = -\cos 2\theta = -\left(1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta\right) = -1 + 2x^{2}$
$2x^{2} - 3x = 0$
$x(2x - 3) = 0$
$x = 0$ OR $x = 3/2$
Only $x = 0$ is valid, so Only 1 solution

questions.stem: Let PQR be a triangle such that $\overrightarrow{PQ} = -2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{PR} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$, $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let S be the point on QR, which is equidistant from the lines PQ and PR. If $|\overrightarrow{PR}| = 9$ and $\overrightarrow{PS} = \hat{i} - 7\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, then the value of $3a - 4b$ is __________.
questions.solution:
PS is internal angle bisector of PQ and PR
$\lambda\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{PR}}{\left|\overrightarrow{PQ}\right|\left|\overrightarrow{PR}\right|}\right) = \overrightarrow{PS}$
$a = 7,\quad b = -4$
But with these values
$\overrightarrow{QS} = \overrightarrow{PS} - \overrightarrow{PQ} = (3, -6, 0)$
$\overrightarrow{SR} = \overrightarrow{PR} - \overrightarrow{PS} = (6, -3, -6)$
$\overrightarrow{QS}$ and $\overrightarrow{SR}$ are not collinear vectors which contradicts the information given in question
$3a - 4b = 3(7) - 4(-4) = 37$
